checks: Proper sections through a common midpoint place that midpoint in the interior. Rotating the signed half-chord vectors gives exactly s_{ji}(z)u_{ji}/2, and the factor ρ/s makes their probability combination vanish.

The accepted planar result therefore gives a 4/9 area fraction for each local weight vector. Subtracting min p from the fractions bounds the loss from a common vector by range times half the ℓ1 distance.

Weighted global cap mass is at most B, and its nonowned contribution is exactly X_j. Owned sets partition the positive bases. The one- and two-cap union bounds justify their zero credits in the group sum.

The objective X_j−E_j is continuous on the finite-dimensional compact simplex. Absolute-value auxiliary variables give a linear program, with their lower bounds attaining the objective even if some penalties are zero.
Proportional lengths cancel the common scalar in each local weight vector, so E_j=0. The source 43df7105059aa4d8 §§3–4 supplies exactly this premise and the same conditional k≤2^n consequence.

dependencies.hypotheses: Translate each owned planar convex body to its interior common chord midpoint. The nonzero opposite endpoints are on its boundary, the positive quarter-turn produces the inward normals, and weighting by normalized ρ/s_{ji}(z) gives zero sum. Thus its ordinary area bound is 4w_z/9.

overlap.comparison: It gives the sharp single-fiber mean for each actual local balancing vector. It does not compare different balancing vectors across owned bases or charge weighted cross-capture.

readability: The symbols p_i for signed half-chord vectors and p_{ji}(z) for fractions are distinct by indexing. The final k≤2^n statement takes n to be the ambient integer dimension.
